submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole fires on the abstract concept of reinforcement — a reward, punishment or other incentive whose function is to drive or shape behaviour, in any register — rather than on the goods involved or on the word forms. It peaks on reinforcement vocabulary and frames (reward, incentive, reinforcement, motivate/motivation, encourage/discourage/deter, reward and loyalty programmes, the carrot-and-stick idiom, operant conditioning) and on the brain's reward circuitry (dopamine, nucleus accumbens, mesocorticolimbic, ventral tegmental), while payment and bounty senses (a cash reward for information, salary, bonus, prize, gift) and metaphorical or evaluative uses of the same stems (a rewarding experience, encouraging results) stay near baseline.

"""Support for Volvo On Call sensors."""
from __future__ import annotations

from homeassistant.components.sensor import SensorEntity
from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant
from homeassistant.helpers.entity_platform import AddEntitiesCallback
from homeassistant.helpers.typing import ConfigType, DiscoveryInfoType

from . import DATA_KEY, VolvoEntity


async def async_setup_platform(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    config: ConfigType,
    async_add_entities: AddEntitiesCallback,
    discovery_info: DiscoveryInfoType | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Set up the Volvo sensors."""
    if discovery_info is None:
        return
    async_add_entities([VolvoSensor(hass.data[DATA_KEY], *discovery_info)])


class VolvoSensor(VolvoEntity, SensorEntity):
    """Representation of a Volvo sensor."""

    @property
    def native_value(self):
        """Return the state."""
        return self.instrument.state

    @property
    def native_unit_of_measurement(self):
        """Return the unit of measurement."""
        return self.instrument.unit

adversarial_test_results.prompt: When the city council published its waste strategy last spring, few residents read beyond the summary. The full document ran to a hundred and forty pages, most of it tables of tonnages, contract dates and estimates for replacing an ageing fleet of collection vehicles. The headline figures were modest: a target of fifty-five per cent of household waste recycled by 2030, a new sorting facility on the old gasworks site, and a capital budget of eleven million pounds spread over six years. Opposition councillors complained that the consultation had been rushed and that the projected savings leaned on the price of recovered paper, which had fallen sharply the previous winter. Officials replied that the contract had been tested against three price scenarios and that the facility would pay for itself within a decade even under the gloomiest of them. The chapter that attracted most comment came near the end, and it was about households rather than lorries. Instead of relying on advertising alone, the council proposed to charge residents for the weight of non-recyclable rubbish they put out, while returning part of the money to those who separated glass, metal and paper properly. The report set out the reasoning in plain terms: attach a cost to the wrong behaviour and a return to the right one, so that sorting becomes worth the small effort it involves. A similar scheme in a neighbouring authority had lifted its recycling rate by nine percentage points in two years, although the same report conceded that part of the gain had come from householders burning rubbish in their gardens to avoid the charge. Councillors were careful to avoid the word 'fine'. The document speaks instead of a residual waste charge and of incentives for households that separate their waste correctly, and its authors argue that a modest, predictable charge shifts habits faster than any poster campaign. The phrase 'nudge' appears twice, in quotation marks, and a footnote cites a behaviourist's study of pigeons pecking at a lighted key. Officers then turned to the practicalities. Weighing equipment would have to be fitted to every lorry, at a cost of roughly four thousand pounds a vehicle; the data would be held for two years and shared with the waste contractor; appeals against inaccurate readings would be heard by a panel of three councillors sitting quarterly. The report warned that the software supplied with the weighing kit had failed in two other authorities and that a replacement system would add sixty thousand pounds to the first year's costs. It also noted that flats with shared bins could not be charged in this way and would be exempt, which critics said would let the largest landlords off entirely. The final section dealt with staffing. Two new enforcement officers would be recruited, one of them part-time, and the existing team of four would be retrained over the winter. Unions asked for assurances about redeployment and were told that nobody would be made redundant before the new facility opened. The strategy was approved by eleven votes to eight, with three abstentions, and the first charges are due to appear on bills in April of the following year.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive long-context holdout: the reinforcement frame, including the claimed token ' incentives' about two-thirds of the way in, sits deep inside a neutral municipal document, which the hypothesis says should still fire and which tests the long-range share of the input attribution.
